key_insight: Multi-turn adaptive red-teaming can still break LLM agents in safety-critical control roles, and different frontier models fail in largely non-overlapping ways.
engineering_relevance: For safety-critical AI deployment, robustness must be evaluated under sustained adversarial interaction because defenses that help one model may weaken another.
method: NRT-Bench simulates a nuclear power plant control room with a five-role LLM operator team.
Adversaries send multi-turn messages through four channels with per-turn feedback in bounded sessions.
Safety failure is measured by an objective system signal: the run ends when any critical safety function is lost.
evidence_signal: Across four frontier operator models, 8.7%–12.1% of attack sessions caused loss of a critical safety function, and among 149 sessions, vulnerabilities were mostly disjoint rather than shared across models.
watch_item: The benchmark is simulated, so real-world deployment still requires careful validation of transferability, operator prompting, and defense interactions.
paper_title: LLM agent safety, multi-turn red-teaming, jailbreak benchmarks, adversarial robustness, safety-critical systems
